turns.text: the elevator on the left has made a noise since tuesday.
does the noise change with the floor, or is it the same one?
is the elevator always this slow before nine in the morning?
it is slower before nine and worse on the days it stops twice.
i pressed four and the door closed on my sleeve.
did the door catch the sleeve, or did you pull it free?
our elevator still smells of a lunch that nobody claimed.
someone left a lunch in there, and the smell has settled.
we were stuck between two and three for four minutes.
four minutes between floors, and nobody had anything to say.
someone held the door for me and i forgot to say thank you.
did the thank you happen at the door, or is it still owed?
the elevator mirror makes me check my hair every morning.
does the mirror on four flatter everyone, or only the early crowd?
the elevator went straight past my floor again.
who looked up when the elevator went past your floor?
two of us looked up and neither of us spoke.
two people looking up is the closest this place gets to a complaint.
our coffee tastes like the pot was cleaned with soap.
did the pot get soap, or does the coffee taste that way now?
the milk sat out overnight and it has turned.
how long was the milk out before someone put it back?
there is a queue for the kettle that starts before the coffee is ready.
people queue for the kettle before the coffee has finished brewing.
the fridge has a smell i cannot place and nobody will claim.
does the smell start in the fridge or on the shelf?
i spilled tea on the counter and wiped it with my sleeve.
did the sleeve work, or did the counter win that round?
who keeps hiding the good mugs behind the chipped ones?
who moved the good mugs, and does anyone own up to it?
our kitchen window does not close and the room is cold by ten.
has the window been open since spring, or does it not close?
the toaster in the kitchen burned my bread and then died.
had the lever gone stiff before it burned the bread?
the lever has been stiff since someone dropped it in the sink.
a dropped toaster explains the bread, and the sink explains the lever.
we have four minutes before the meeting starts and no agenda.
invent an agenda in four minutes, or walk in without one?
an email would have done the job, and everyone here knows it.
would anyone in the room believe that email was the better option?
do we start with the good news and stop before lunch?
can we end before lunch, or does the good news run long?
i have been in this room for six hours and the clock is wrong.
why is the clock wrong, and have we really been here six hours?
the first slide has a typo and nobody has mentioned it.
someone should mention the typo before the slide goes out.
do we need introductions again, or does everyone know everyone?
introductions cost four minutes and prevent an hour of guessing.
our projector is on the blink and the backup one is missing.
the projector blinks at the worst slide, the backup left in june.
can we do my part of the meeting first, since i stop at eleven?
does eleven mean eleven, or does your part need a slow exit?
eleven means eleven, and i will be walking out mid sentence.
walking out mid sentence is a habit this room respects.
a new person on my floor has a plant and no computer.
what is the plant called, or is it too early for names?
i showed the new coworker where the printer lives and she wrote it down.
writing down the printer is the mark of someone who has been burned.
does the new hire know that the friday meeting runs long?
nobody warns the new hire, and friday runs long regardless.
my new coworker asked who signs off on the building passes.
the passes go through reception, and reception has never said no.
the new starter sits at my old cubicle and the chair still squeaks.
why does the chair squeak for her and not for me?
i gave the new person the short version of the coffee rules.
did the short version cover the good mugs or the washing up?
is the new colleague coming to the thursday lunch or eating at her desk?
she is coming, and she has already been warned about thursday.
the new colleague has a name tag that says trainee.
does anyone ever take the trainee tag off, or does it stay?
mine said trainee for a month and nobody ever changed it.
twice introduced, and the tag stays trainee until someone notices.
they are moving our floor to the building across the road in march.
has anyone packed a box, or are we all waiting for march?
my desk goes to the window side and the plants stay behind.
the window side gets the light, and the plants will notice.
the movers arrive on friday and we have to label everything.
label the kettle first, because the kettle is what people look for.
do we keep the same desk number or does the office renumber everything?
will the desk number stay, or does everything change with it?
our new floor has fewer windows and a much smaller kitchen.
fewer windows is a loss, and the smaller kitchen is a bigger one.
someone has already put a name card on my new cubicle.
a name card is waiting there, which saves the first morning.
we lose the good meeting room and gain a corner with a screen.
will the corner with a screen be booked solid within a week?
the move date has slipped twice and the boxes are still empty.
twice slipped, and does anyone trust the march date now?
nobody believes march, but we all keep writing it on the forms.
the forms will say march long after the boxes arrive in april.
our holiday party is at the same place as last year.
how did the party land in the same room as last year?
are we doing secret santa again or did we learn our lesson?
we are doing it again, and nobody has learned the lesson.
i have been asked to bring the same dip i brought last year.
does anyone expect the same dip again, or can i change it?
the party starts at seven and the last train is at ten.
ten gives you three hours, and that is two hours too many.
does the party have a dress code or is it the usual office clothes?
the usual office clothes, and one person will still wear a tie.
i am on the party committee and we have met once.
has the committee met once, or was that the party itself?
the party food ran out before nine last year.
nine is early for a food shortage, and the sandwiches went first.
someone brings a guitar and someone asks for a song, every year.
a guitar arrives and the room politely waits for it to stop.
david has a retirement do on friday in the room by the stairs.
has david asked for no speeches, or is that just talk?
i have been asked to say a few words and i have written none.
have you written any of the words yet, or is friday the plan?
he has been here thirty years and the badge photo is from the first one.
has anyone taken a new badge photo in thirty years?
we are collecting for a gift and the envelope is in the kitchen.
the envelope sits in the kitchen, and nobody knows what to buy.
is anyone bringing a card for him to sign or is the gift enough?
what carries more weight here, the card or the gift?
he said he will not miss the meetings and everyone laughed.
the meetings will not be missed, and the laugh was honest.
the retirement card has forty signatures and half of them are illegible.
forty signatures and only four names anyone can read, which is normal.
my ride in took forty minutes and the last mile was slow.
why is the last mile always the slow one, and was today worse?
i leave at seven and the road is clear for exactly twenty minutes.
does the road stay clear for twenty minutes, or is that luck?
the walk from the station is fine until it rains.
a wet walk adds ten minutes and takes away the good mood.
i read on the way in and i have finished two books this month.
two books in a month says the journey is longer than the job.
does the early start bother you or are you used to it now?
the early start stopped bothering me in the second week, honestly.
our road has been dug up since january.
keeping a road half closed since january takes patience from everyone.
i missed my stop by two stations and walked back in the rain.
did you walk back from the next station in the rain?
the printer on our floor has been out of paper since monday.
does anyone own the printer refill, or is it everybody and nobody?
our copier jams every time i send a double sided job.
send it single sided and the machine has nothing to argue about.
there is a sign on the printer that says out of order.
how long has that sign been up, and does it still count?
our post room closes at four and nobody told the new floor.
why does the post room close at four, and who agreed to it?
my parcel has been in the post room since tuesday.
when did the parcel arrive, and who signed for it?
do we sign for our own deliveries or does reception do it?
does reception sign, or does the post room hand it over?
a visitor asked me where the nearest coffee is.
send the visitor to the machine on two and apologize in advance.
the reception desk has no one on it after five.
who covers the desk after five, and do they know it?
our visitor badges are the same color as the staff ones.
does the badge color matter, or does the lanyard give it away?
our car park fills before eight every single morning.
eight is when the permit holders stop being polite about it.
i circled twice and then parked on the top level.
how often did you circle before you took the top level?
my permit runs out this month and i have not renewed.
renew the permit now, because the queue at month end is long.
a van took two spaces this morning and left.
did anyone see the van, or did it leave without a word?
we are on the stairs all week while the elevator is fixed.
how many floors do the stairs cover, and does anyone count?
i met three people on the stairs who never take them.
do people on the stairs ever say anything, or just nod?
does anyone know when the stairs stop smelling of paint?
the paint dries eventually, which the sign did not promise.
our canteen queue starts before the doors open.
does the queue ever move early, or is the schedule fixed?
they ran out of the soup by half past twelve.
half past twelve is late to expect soup and a seat.
my lunch break is thirty minutes and the queue is twenty.
twenty of thirty on a queue leaves ten for the food.
our fire drill is scheduled for thursday at ten.
does the drill expect us to read the signs first?
we stood outside for twenty minutes in the cold.
did twenty minutes outside cover everyone, or was someone missing?
does the drill count if half the floor is at lunch?
half a floor at lunch means the drill counts twice next time.
the recycling bin is full of coffee cups by lunchtime.
cups go in the bin and the lid never quite closes after.
i put a pizza box in and it was fished out again.
a clean box goes in paper and a greasy one goes elsewhere.
there are three bins and none of them are labeled.
who labeled the three bins, and did anyone read the labels?
who empties the bins on this floor and when?
do facilities come on fridays, or when the bins ask?
the heating on our side comes on at six and stays on.
does the heating ever go off, or does six run until six?
my desk is under a vent and the air never warms up.
the vent was meant for a different desk layout entirely.
can we open a window, or does the building keep us sealed?
does a window actually open, or does the seal come from above?
our booking system gave my desk to someone else.
does the system apologize, or does it just move the desk?
i booked the same desk for the whole week.
does a week in one seat hold, or does the system forget?
do we book a desk before we travel or after?
book before, because after is how the good seats vanish.
the conference line dropped twice during the call.
did the line come back, or did we talk over the gap?
nobody on the call knew the dial in code.
where is the code kept, and does anyone check it?
can you hear me now, or is it still cutting out?
i can hear you now, but the line still drops on long calls.
the line went quiet and we all waited for the host.
a quiet line means the host is reading something long out loud.
he came back and asked where we had got to.
how far had we got before the line came back?
our training session is three hours and has no break.
does three hours include a break, or is that too much to ask?
the training video ran forty minutes for six slides.
did six slides need forty minutes, or did the video stall?
do we get a certificate when the training finishes?
does the certificate go on the wall, or in a drawer?
my review is on friday and i have nothing prepared.
friday gives you three days to find two good examples.
the review form asks for three goals for next year.
do three goals fit the year, or does the form just want numbers?
does the review cover a full year or just the last quarter?
the form says a year and the questions ask about october.
we are passing a card around for priya on friday.
a card on friday means the collection needs to start today.
the card has sat on my desk since monday.
how long has the card sat there, and who has signed?
how much do we usually put in for a leaving gift?
does five each cover the gift, or do we pass it twice?
my coat has been on the hook since november.
a coat on a hook for a season is furniture now.
the cloakroom is full and the hooks are all taken.
hooks fill up and the last one always goes to a scarf.
do we leave bags in the cloakroom overnight?
overnight is fine until somebody needs the room at seven.
someone moved my bag to the shelf by the door.
the shelf by the door is where bags go to be forgotten.
my password expired and the reset link did not arrive.
did the reset link ever arrive, or is it still out there?
the new password rules need a number and a symbol.
a number and a symbol make a password nobody can recall.
do i call the service desk or raise a ticket?
does a ticket get answered faster than a call to the desk?
my building pass stopped working at the side door.
did the side door even read it, or just refuse the pass?
we need a pass for the storage room on four.
ask facilities and bring your own pass to trade for it.
does the pass work in the other building as well?
does the other building take the same pass, or a second one?
the coffee rota says my name on thursday.
thursday is yours, and the milk runs out before you arrive.
we have not had a rota since june.
the rota stopped in june and nobody wrote a name after.
who buys the milk when the rota runs out?
whoever notices the milk first buys it and complains for a week.
the noticeboard still has a poster from the summer fair.
how old is that poster, and does anyone still read it?
a note on the board says the room is closed.
the note and the room disagree, and the note is winning.
do we still put paper notices on the board?
paper notices stay up long after everyone has read them.
the board by the stairs is the one everyone walks past.
the stairs board gets read and the corridor one gets dust.
the charity collection tin is on the kitchen counter.
how much is in the tin, and does anyone keep count?
we are doing a bake sale for the collection on friday.
does a bake sale beat the tin, or is it more effort?
does the company match what we raise for the charity?
the match is capped and the form for it is not obvious.
the collection total was read out in the meeting.
who read the total out in the meeting, and did anyone clap?
someone warmed fish for lunch and the floor knows.
the fish smell reaches every corner of the floor before lunch.
my soup burst in the microwave and i left it.
did anyone clean the soup, or does the next person find it?
there is a splatter in the microwave from a chili made in march.
does the chili splatter come off, or is it permanent art now?
at noon the microwave line starts and it ends at one.
the line moves one plate at a time, and everyone reheats in shifts.
someone burned popcorn and the alarm nearly went off.
how close was the popcorn to setting the alarm off for everyone?
our microwave door only closes if you lift and push.
the door needs the lift first, and the push comes second.
i wiped the microwave yesterday and the splatters are back.
how long did the clean microwave last before the splatters returned?
the microwave on our floor died and the one upstairs is foreign.
does the upstairs microwave take the same plates, or different ones?
it takes different plates and the turntable is missing.
a missing turntable means every plate spins by hand up there.
the vending machine swallowed my dollar and gave nothing back.
does the machine pay out eventually, or does the dollar count as charity?
our snack drawer has the same granola bars since last summer.
how old is a granola bar before anyone admits it is stale?
someone keeps restocking the vending machine with the coffee candy.
who buys the coffee candy, and does anyone actually like it?
that vending machine gives two bars when you press b four.
the double bars happen every time, and mondays are no exception.
our floor has a candy jar that nobody refills.
who refilled the candy jar last, and when was that?
everything in the vending machine is gone except the pretzels.
the pretzels are that bad, and the machine is protecting them.
i keep a chocolate bar in my desk for emergencies.
what counts as an emergency for the desk chocolate, a monday?
the supply closet is locked and nobody has the key.
who held the key last, and did they leave the building?
all the good pens vanish within a week of arriving.
where do the good pens go, and does anyone return them?
our floor stapler has been jammed since easter.
nobody fixes the stapler, and it jams forever by choice.
we order envelopes once a year and run out by may.
does may arrive early, or do the envelopes leave in bulk?
our label maker is the most borrowed item in the office.
the label maker travels the floor and never comes back the same day.
someone labeled the closet shelves and now nothing is where it was.
did the labels describe the shelves, or invent a new system?
the hole punch only works if you hold it upside down.
the hole punch works upside down for everyone, by now.
i found a drawer of pencils from a company that no longer exists.
does the old company name come off the pencils, or stay?
the name is printed on every single pencil.
printed pencils outlive the company, which is more than branding usually does.
our dress code says smart casual and nobody agrees what it means.
what does smart casual look like on a monday, in practice?
friday is dress down and someone still wears a tie.
the tie on friday means a meeting, or a habit nobody breaks.
i wore jeans on a tuesday and got two comments.
do two comments on jeans count as a policy, or an opinion?
the new dress code arrived as a pdf nobody opened.
nobody opened the pdf, and the old code stands by default.
our client visits mean suits, and the suits live at the dry cleaner.
does the dry cleaner know the suits only work twice a month?
someone came in slippers and called them office shoes.
the slippers passed inspection, and the day forgave them quietly.
the thermostat war is the only dress code we follow.
does the thermostat decide the layers, or do the layers win?
our office days are tuesday and wednesday, chosen by a survey.
does the survey ask the quiet people, or only the keen ones?
monday at home puts the meetings in pajama bottoms.
the pajama meetings count, and the camera stays off by rule.
the office is half empty on mondays and full on wednesdays.
why does the office fill on wednesdays, when mondays exist too?
my home desk is a kitchen table and my chair is a stool.
the stool survives until three, and then the table takes over.
the dog attends every home meeting and has opinions.
does the dog get an agenda item, or just the camera?
we have a rule that cameras stay on for the first five minutes.
the cameras stay on after five, and everyone fades out politely.
a day without a train is worth two hours of sleep.
what gets done with the two hours, sleep or the laundry?
i have worked from home so long the office plants forgot me.
do the plants recover, or do they hold a grudge?
the fern by the window died and the rest survived.
the fern was the honest one, and the rest just waited.
the company meeting is at four on a friday, as tradition demands.
does friday at four keep the questions short, or end them?
our chief executive takes questions and nobody asks any.
does the silence mean respect, or do the questions go elsewhere?
our company meeting has a slide with the birthdays on it.
the birthday slide gets read out, and the scrolling never happens.
the same person asks a question every single month.
the monthly question never surprises anyone, and that is the tradition.
our company meeting ran twenty minutes over and the cookies ran out.
did the cookies go before the end, or with the overtime?
someone clapped at the sales numbers and it caught on.
the clapping for the numbers continued, and one quarter was enough.
the town hall questions are screened and everyone knows it.
does a screened question still count as a question at the end?
the screening keeps the awkward ones out and the soft ones in.
soft questions keep the hour short, which may be the point.
the forecast says rain every day this week and it delivers.
does the rain ever take a lunch break, or is it constant?
first frost this morning and the sidewalk was a rink.
did anyone stay upright on the sidewalk, or did the frost win?
this heat wave turned the office into a greenhouse by noon.
the greenhouse office holds the heat until the cleaners leave.
i checked three forecast apps and got three different answers.
the first of the three apps gets the blame when it rains.
the window by my desk shows weather and nothing else.
what does the window show when the weather runs out?
snow closed the schools and the office stayed open.
the office closes for floods, and the snow can wait outside.
the umbrella stand fills by nine and empties by five.
one umbrella walks off every winter, and the stand forgives it.
weather small talk is the only talk before nine here.
does the pre nine talk go past the weather, ever?
the food truck comes on tuesdays and the line is long.
does the truck line move, or does tuesday test patience?
that sandwich place raised prices and kept the same bread.
the same bread does not justify the new prices, sadly.
our new cafe has better coffee and worse chairs.
which wins a second visit, the coffee or the chairs?
our lunch walk is fifteen minutes and the food is five.
does the walk justify the food, or the food the walk?
my deli knows my order and starts it when i walk in.
the deli order never changes, and the deli prefers it that way.
nobody mentions the free bread at the salad place.
the free bread is a secret, and everyone keeps it politely.
a taco truck claimed the corner when the burger truck left.
the taco truck holds the spot, and the rotation rumor is false.
i brought lunch from home and everyone asked about the smell.
did the smell read as a compliment, or a complaint in disguise?
the lunch debate is the same four places every day.
do the four places ever grow to five, or is four the limit?
someone suggested the place by the bridge and it was rejected.
the bridge place waits a year, then joins the four.
the radio in our kitchen plays one station and nobody changes it.
does anyone dare change the station, or is it fixed by fear?
someone brought a speaker for the office and it never leaves their desk.
the speaker never leaves that desk, which makes the desk its home.
our playlist is one person choosing and everyone else listening.
one person chooses the playlist, and everyone pays in patience.
our radio gets turned up at four and down at five.
does the volume at four have a reason, or just a habit?
i brought headphones and the office went quiet around me.
the headphones end the radio debate for one person at a time.
the friday playlist is different and nobody knows who sets it.
who sets the friday playlist, and can they be thanked?
someone hums along to every song and every commercial.
the humming follows every song and every commercial without a gap.
our radio broke and the silence lasted one morning.
did the silence feel like peace, or like a missing limb?
by lunch someone was humming the station jingle from memory.
a jingle from memory outlives the radio that played it.
my desk plant has survived three desks and two office moves.
what keeps the plant going through moves that lose everything else?
our succulent on the window sill drinks nothing and thrives.
does the succulent ever need water, or is neglect the trick?
someone waters every plant on the floor and claims no credit.
someone waters the plants on a schedule nobody sees or praises.
that palm by the window gets the best light and the least attention.
does the palm prefer the light, or the quiet of the corner?
i named my desk plant and now i cannot let it go.
a named plant outlives every desk it sits on, apparently.
the office bought twelve plants and six survived the winter.
the six survivors kept their spots, and the winter got the rest.
our office watering can vanished and the plants noticed first.
does the watering can come back, or do the plants adapt?
a plant two desks away outgrew its pot and got a bucket.
the bucket counts as a promotion, with room to grow.
our birthday cake lives in the kitchen from eleven until it is gone.
does the cake survive past one, or is eleven its peak?
we sing for the birthday person and nobody knows the second verse.
the singing stops at the first verse, and the muddling starts there.
our cake schedule says i bake for the next birthday in march.
the march cake flavor stays a surprise, even from the baker.
someone always writes the wrong name on the cake.
does the wrong name get corrected, or just eaten around?
this office skips the singing and goes straight to the cake.
skipping the singing saves four minutes and a little dignity.
that birthday list on the fridge has three names and two are wrong.
who fixes the birthday list, or does it stay a rumor?
i baked for the office once and the standard was set too high.
the standard survives, and a store cake would be noticed.
the birthday card goes around a week early and returns unsigned.
does the card come back signed, or does one person carry it?
it came back with two signatures and one belonged to the birthday person.
signing your own card is the honest end of the birthday card.
our run club has three members and one of them is fast.
does the fast one wait at the corner, or finish alone?
the office gym has two treadmills and one works.
the one working treadmill gets booked, then fought over anyway.
i joined the gym at work and went twice in a year.
twice in a year counts as visiting, with an honest membership.
our showers at the gym have one hook and no shelf.
does the hook hold the towel, the clothes, or the hope?
the run club meets at noon and returns at different times.
the run club scatters at noon and reassembles by the door.
my gym towel disappeared and a new one appeared in its place.
the new towel counts as a trade, and nobody mentions it.
the yoga class at lunch has six spots and ten takers.
do the four without spots wait by the door, or give up?
two waited by the door and got spots when two left early.
waiting by the door is the office version of a standby flight.
my expense report came back because one receipt was blurry.
does the blurry receipt need a reprint, or a better camera?
the mileage claim asks for the route and i drive the same one.
the same route gets retyped every time, by the same person.
our approvals go through three people and one is on vacation.
does the report wait for the vacation, or go to the other people?
i claimed a coffee and the form asked for a business reason.
no business reason fits a coffee on a tuesday, honestly.
the finance team returns reports on fridays, like a delivery.
the reports come back friday, and the fixes land on monday.
the per diem covers lunch but not the coffee that got me through.
the per diem has never met a deadline, let alone a coffee.
a report from our team was rejected for a missing decimal point.
the decimal point gets found, and the report resubmitted in june.
i saved every receipt for six weeks and lost the envelope.
does the envelope turn up, or do six weeks of receipts restart?
my hotel for the conference was next to the train station.
did the station hotel get any sleep, or just the noise?
my flight was at six in the morning and the taxi came at four.
does the four am taxi count as travel, or as punishment?
the conference had forty talks and i understood three.
does the conference badge matter more than the three talks?
my per diem for the trip bought one dinner and six coffees.
does the coffee count as dinner on the second night?
that airport line moved slower than the flight itself.
the line deserves the complaint, and the flight gets the sympathy.
i packed for two days and stayed for four.
does day four get a laundry run, or a new shirt?
our hotel breakfast ended at nine and my alarm was wrong.
the alarm cost the breakfast, and room service charged for the rescue.
the return flight was delayed and the terminal ran out of seats.
does a delayed flight make the terminal a hotel, or a waiting room?
i found a seat by the window and guarded it for two hours.
a guarded seat by the window is the only real estate here.
our suggestion box has not been opened since the last office move.
does anyone open the box, or is it furniture now?
someone suggested a second microwave and got a reply in a year.
does a year feel long for a second microwave, or fair?
those anonymous suggestions are less anonymous than the writers think.
does the handwriting betray the anonymous suggestions, or the complaint?
my suggestion about the heating got a thank you and no heating.
the thank you counts as closure, which is a different thing from action.
our box by the door collects suggestions and spare change.
does the spare change get counted, or join the suggestions?
someone suggested fewer meetings and the meeting grew longer.
does the longer meeting answer the suggestion, or bury it?
the suggestions get read out once a year at the company meeting.
does the reading of suggestions happen before the cake, or after?
i put a suggestion in the box and heard nothing for months.
does the silence around a suggestion mean no, or maybe?
a reply arrived pinned to the noticeboard, addressed to no one.
a reply addressed to no one is how the office answers.
our office newsletter has one pun headline and no news.
does the pun carry the newsletter, or bury the news?
the newsletter announces babies, marriages, and one promotion a year.
the promotion gets a paragraph, and the babies get the page.
i was in the newsletter once for winning a raffle.
does the raffle fame fade, or does it follow you?
each newsletter comes out on the first monday of the month.
does the first monday hold, or does the newsletter drift?
someone writes the newsletter anonymously and everyone knows who.
does everyone know who writes it, or just pretend not to?
our team photo in the newsletter has three people who left.
the photo stays a museum piece, updated once per building move.
the newsletter asked for contributions and got one recipe.
one recipe counts as a response, and as a quiet warning.
our bookshelf works on trust and the trust is holding.
how many books have walked off the bookshelf this year?
someone left a note in a novel instead of a bookmark.
the note counts as a review, and nobody has claimed it.
that shelf has three copies of the same cookbook.
does anyone cook from the cookbook, or just donate it?
i finished a book from the shelf and felt obliged to replace it.
the replacement book matches the gap, and improves on it.
our bookshelf is the only furniture nobody has complained about.
what keeps the bookshelf safe from every single office reorganization?
someone donated a whole encyclopedia set from 1994.
the encyclopedia set holds the shelf down, and everyone lets them.
